body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Description

When using `torch._inductor.config.graph_partition = True`, an unbacked SymInt (`u0`) returned from a `cudagraph_unsafe` custom op is threaded into a cudagraph-safe partition. That partition then uses `u0` in CUDA allocation shapes and pointer offsets (via `reinterpret_tensor`), making the
partition itself not cudagraph-safe.

### Expected Behavior

With `graph_partition=True`, the graph should split such that cudagraph-safe partitions not depend on unbacked SymInts for their shapes/strides/offsets. In particular, partition should contain only fixed-shape GEMMs (like `dummy_ops1`, `dummy_ops2`) and should remain capturable. The data-dependent GEMMs should be tagged unsafe and moved out of partition.


### Repro

```python
import os

os.environ["TORCH_LOGS"] = "+output_code"

import torch
import torch._dynamo
import torch._inductor.config

torch._inductor.config.graph_partition = True
torch._dynamo.config.capture_dynamic_output_shape_ops = True

device = "cuda"
dtype = torch.bfloat16

B = 256
D_IN = 512
D_OUT = 4096

def create_model():
    W1 = torch.randn(D_IN, D_OUT, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    W2 = torch.randn(D_OUT, D_IN, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    @torch.compile(backend="inductor", mode="reduce-overhead", fullgraph=True)
    def forward(q: torch.Tensor):
        dummy_ops1 = W1 @ W2
        dummy_ops2 = q @ W1

        num_decode = torch.ops.reprolib.get_split_point(q) # Returns unbacked SymInt

        torch._check(num_decode >= 0)
        torch._check(num_decode <= q.shape[0])

        num_prefill = q.shape[0] - num_decode

        decode_q = q.narrow(0, 0, num_decode)
        prefill_q = q.narrow(0, num_decode, num_prefill)

        # BUG: The GEMMs should be outside the cudagraph-safe partitions
        prefill_out = prefill_q @ W1
        prefill_out2 = prefill_out @ W2

        decode_out = decode_q @ W1

        return dummy_ops1, dummy_ops2, prefill_out2, decode_out

    return forward

# Custom op returning SymInt, tagged cudagraph_unsafe
lib = torch.library.Library("reprolib", "FRAGMENT")
lib.define("get_split_point(Tensor x) -> SymInt", tags=[torch._C.Tag.cudagraph_unsafe])

@torch.library.impl(lib, "get_split_point", "CUDA")
def get_split_point_impl(x):
    return 64  # Simulates data-dependent value


@torch.library.register_fake("reprolib::get_split_point")
def get_split_point_fake(x):
    ctx = torch.library.get_ctx()
    return ctx.new_dynamic_size(min=0, max=B)


if __name__=="__main__":
    q = torch.randn(B, D_IN, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    model = create_model()
    torch.compiler.cudagraph_mark_step_begin()
    _, _, out1, out2 = model(q)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
```


### Error logs

Output Code: [op_code.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24690821/op_code.py)

- `get_split_point` returns an unbacked symint and is manually tagged cudagraph-unsafe. So it doesn't appear inside `partition_0`.
- `extern_kernels.mm(reinterpret_tensor(arg2_1, (256 + ((-1)*u0), 512), (512, 1), 512*u0), arg0_1, out=buf5)` these matrix multiplication op (with data dependency) should be considered cudagraph-unsafe and shouldn't be inside `partition_0`

comments.body: @therealnaveenkamal @ProExpertProg @ezyang I am working on it. would try to come up with a fix soon
I have raised the PR for this issue. PTAL @therealnaveenkamal @ezyang @ProExpertProg @zou3519 @BoyuanFeng

@therealnaveenkamal we have `cudagraph_skip_dynamic_graphs` to skip dynamic shapes in cudagraph regions. we could similarly add a skip for unbacked shapes only. 

But i'm not sure the current behavior is a bug ? there's nothing unsafe about taking in an unbacked int. cc @BoyuanFeng

@ProExpertProg yes, agreed we should add an api for tagging particular symints. In this instance, it's perhaps unprofitable, but it's not unsafe, since we add guards/respecialize for each unique input.

@eellison this might be due to vLLM dropping guards but where does the specialization happen? Because we did not see it happen and so the answer was wrong because the data-dependent shapes got locked into cudagraphs.

Hoping to discuss adding this API at the Thursday sync.

There is a mismatch between pt cudagraph_tree and vllm CUDAGraphWrapper

The graph partition signature is

```python
def partition_0(args):
    arg0_1, arg1_1, arg2_1, buf0, u0 = args
    ...
```

PT2 cudagraph tree collects all ints in the arguments (`u0` in this example) and find the corresponding cudagraph.

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/3599c9635acb782646195fcfa0c1d6b7e7773d9f/torch/_inductor/cudagraph_trees.py#L413-L418


In vLLM, we wrap CUDAGraphWrapper on `partition_0`. It does not check all ints in the arguments (thus ignoring `u0`). It assumes the only dynamic shape is batch size and only checks the `batch_descriptor` (aka batch size).

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/aaf4b70aae5976115eb5f8caead3d4eeb3657136/vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py#L231


Going forward, we can mark an unbacked symint as cg unsafe and exclude all related ops.
cc @laithsakka any thoughts on an API that marks specific `SymInt`s as cudagraph-unsafe?
If we are good with adding the ability to mark specific symints as cudgraph-unsafe, @ayushsatyam146 has bandwidth to implement the feature.

> API that marks specific `SymInt`s as cudagraph-unsafe?
@ProExpertProg the idea is fine for me,BUT, 

Can we use terminology other than safe / unsafe for dynamic shapes that are allowed or not allowed in CUDA graphs?

It seems like everything is “safe” in the sense of correctness, but Inductor will perform dynamic dispatch on dynamic shapes and recapture the graph. What we want is to control when to allow dynamic shapes in a CUDA graph.

Maybe something like cudagraph_capturable? For example:

torch._dynamo.set_cudagraph_capturable(s0/u0, True/False)

Also, just for clarification: when s0 is not cudagraph_capturable, we will skip the entire graph containing it if graph_partition=False. If graph_partition=True, we will split the graph—i.e., find the maximal subgraph that does not include s0 and CUDA-graph that part This is something that happens automatically in Inductor, right, and not something vLLM has to handle manually? is my understanding correct? @BoyuanFeng @eellison

We also need to think when this annotations happens, the easiest idea would be to mark the symint as cudagraph safe/unsafe upon creation (or included/excluded - sorry laith). But I guess then we're mixing concerns a little bit

I feel the confusion here mostly stems around the fact that we occasionally do support dynamic shapes with cudagraphs (batch size, by retracing the cudagraph for multiple sizes). In principle, if you had a cuda graph unsafe op that returned a tensor of size u0, the extent processing this u0 COULD be cudagraphed if you were willing to record cudagraphs for multiple distinct values of u0. Is this actually a good idea? Well with multiple symbols you will quickly get an explosion of possible combos, so maybe not.

If you only care about identifying the batch dynamic symbol, life is relatively simple: there is one symbol which is OK to cudagraph and all the other symbols are not OK. The API here ought to be related to whatever is also setting up the dispatch/record multiple graphs per size.

@BoyuanFeng If the batch size is the only “CUDA graph–safe” dynamic dimension, then we can add an argument to mark_dynamic and mark_unbacked as well, and disallow everything else.

Are there any other dynamic shapes we want to allow in CUDA graphs for the vLLM use case?

> Are there any other dynamic shapes we want to allow in CUDA graphs for the vLLM use case?

Not that I know of, because we currently have a linear amount of cudagraphs and with any other size we'd get a quadratic amount which is unsustainable. The only other case would be if a symint is constrained to the batch size but hopefully then we can express it in terms of batch size directly. For example, if we want to pad the batch size to a multiple of 4 for specific ops, we'd want to make sure that works correctly and doesn't get ops excluded from cudagraphs.

The only other case would be if a symint is constrained to the batch size but hopefully then we can express it in terms of batch size directly. For example, if we want to pad the batch size to a multiple of 4 for specific ops, we'd want to make sure that works correctly and doesn't get ops excluded from cudagraphs.

if we did padding the size will be a function of the batch size, i dont think that would be an issue.

title: [torch.compile][Bug] Unbacked SymInt leaks into a cudagraph-safe partitions
